pagina_01:
Create PAGE 1 of a three-page Brazilian Portuguese fantasy comic, a polished finished vertical comic page, portrait aspect ratio roughly 2:3, rich hand-painted graphic-novel art with confident ink contours, expressive readable characters and beautifully detailed woodland. NOT pixel art, NOT a screenshot, NOT a game UI. Reference image is ONLY for the woodland palette and the BLUE-SHIRT PLAYER near the lower center; do NOT draw the beige-shirt NPC, shelter, interface or any text from the reference.
Series title in a restrained top title strip: "ALGOLAND". Chapter heading: "CAPÍTULO 1 — O CHÃO". Small page number 1 at bottom.
Canonical protagonist for all pages: young adult man about 22, warm medium-light skin, short tousled chestnut-brown hair, brown eyes, clean-shaven, plain faded BLUE short-sleeve shirt with a simple laced neckline, dark brown trousers, worn brown leather ankle boots. No cloak, no armor, no weapons, no backpack yet. Natural human proportions, consistent face and clothes in every panel. Camera may change freely, not limited to game top-down. Lush green forest, warm brown earth, ferns, moss, subtle pale mint invocation light, daylight through canopy. Never show an enormous sacred tree, another person, a god or a portal doorway; the source of the calling is mysterious.
SIX clearly separated panels, left-to-right top-to-bottom, calm pacing, cream gutters and legible Portuguese narration boxes inset generously from edges. 1 wide top panel, 2 panels second row, 2 panels third row, 1 wide bottom panel. All text must be exactly the following, no extra narration.
Panel 1 wide: extreme close-up of one little green leaf floating UPWARD with a few others behind, forest canopy blurred in depth, beautiful restrained wonder. Caption: "A primeira coisa que vi foi uma folha subindo."
Panel 2: three-quarter full-body protagonist suspended a short distance over a pale green glowing patch of earth, feet seeking footing, startled but not comical. Caption: "A luz estava debaixo de mim."
Panel 3: protagonist lands on both knees, his right palm bracing on brown soil, small dust puff. The fall is low and survivable. Caption: "Os joelhos atingiram a terra."
Panel 4: close-up of his right hand pressing dirt; thin mint light runs through one ordinary exposed root and fades into bark. Caption: "Por um instante, linhas claras correram pelo chão."
Panel 5: intimate close view of his face as he raises his head, kneeling amid fallen leaves; the light is now gone. Caption: "Levantei a cabeça. Ninguém."
Panel 6 wide: rear three-quarter shot of same protagonist now standing and following a small dirt track toward a weathered wooden post bearing a tattered BLUE cloth with a WHITE TREE EMBLEM. A CLOSED small iron-bound wooden rescue chest sits beside the post; tiny stream glimpsed far left through foliage. Daylight and deep forest continue naturally. Caption: "Então fui até o poste."
Editorial priorities: reading order, cinematic continuity, no duplicated protagonist within one panel, correct hands, plants visibly belong to the same forest across panels. Portuguese lettering large, clean, high contrast; keep narration short and avoid covering faces or hands. This is a readable comic page, no dense paragraphs.
pagina_02:
Create PAGE 2, a NEW finished portrait comic page continuing the supplied PAGE 1 reference. This is the start of Chapter 2 of AlgoLand. Match EXACTLY the illustration style, cream gutters, black panel borders, typesetting, woodland, main character facial identity, blue laced shirt, brown trousers, brown boots, and rescue chest / blue cloth WHITE TREE banner seen in PAGE 1. No pixel art and no game HUD. Do not repeat page 1's events.
Top title strip: "ALGOLAND" and "CAPÍTULO 2 — PARA QUEM CHEGA". Small page number 2 at the bottom. Only one protagonist, same young adult clean-shaven chestnut-haired man. Daylight forest; stream remains to the LEFT of the post. Brown iron-bound rescue chest beside post on dry ground. Maintain character equipment chronology: no weapons in panels 1-3 until he retrieves them, then steel sword with plain iron crossguard in his RIGHT hand and battered ROUND wooden shield with iron rim strapped to LEFT forearm. No cloak, armor or bags.
SIX panels with clean left-to-right reading order: two small panels top row, one wide discovery panel middle, two medium panels next row, one wide bottom suspense panel. Narration in generous cream boxes with legible black Brazilian Portuguese lettering; reproduce the following EXACT text and no extra text.
Panel 1: close-up of protagonist's hand testing the chest's metal clasp, chest closed. Caption: "Não estava trancado."
Panel 2: he leans over and raises the heavy wooden lid using BOTH hands, effort in shoulders, hinges creak. Small sound effect: "CRÉÉC". Caption: "A tampa resistiu no começo."
Panel 3 WIDE: over-the-shoulder view into open chest showing ONE plain steel sword and ONE round wooden iron-rimmed shield nestled neatly into fitted compartments. His face partially visible, surprised and relieved. Caption: "Dentro havia uma espada e um escudo."
Panel 4: he stands beside open chest lifting the sword with his RIGHT hand, blade angles down under its weight, LEFT arm still bare, no shield yet. Caption: "O peso puxou meu braço."
Panel 5: close-up of him tightening the shield's INNER leather straps around his LEFT forearm using his right hand; sword has been temporarily laid visibly across the open chest, not floating. Round wooden shield faces outward, correct functional hand grip. Caption: "Apertei as correias, uma de cada vez."
Panel 6 WIDE: dramatic woodland clearing view, protagonist seen three-quarter from behind at left, NOW with sword RIGHT hand and round shield LEFT arm. He faces a SMALL ROOT CREATURE emerging from brush beyond the banner at right. Creature is about waist-to-chest high, hunched knot of gnarled brown tree-root wood, pointed bark plates, a little amber resin glow in its chest, two long clawed root arms and root-like feet. This is a common rebento, NOT a huge humanoid tree boss. One claw parts foliage, creature threatens, hasn't struck yet. Match game's root-monster identity. Caption: "Foi quando alguma coisa se moveu além do poste."
Clarity and continuity over visual clutter. No duplicated swords or shields, no extra fingers, correct limbs and hands. Do not change the protagonist into another person. Keep lettering large, crisp and comfortably inside frames. Premium fantasy graphic novel illustration, dramatic but natural lighting, lush foliage, emotional readable faces.
pagina_03:
Create PAGE 3, the final page of Chapter 2 in a three-page AlgoLand comic. Use supplied PAGE 2 as strict continuity reference: SAME young adult chestnut-haired protagonist, SAME faded blue short-sleeve laced shirt, dark brown trousers, brown boots, SAME simple steel sword in RIGHT hand and ROUND wooden iron-rimmed shield strapped to LEFT forearm. Match facial identity, forest, root monster, rescue post, blue banner bearing white tree, open chest, ink drawing and painted colors, cream gutters and lettering. Premium finished fantasy comic, portrait 2:3, NOT game pixel art.
Header "ALGOLAND" and "CAPÍTULO 2 — PARA QUEM CHEGA". Bottom page number 3.
Continue exactly where page 2 ends: first encounter against ONE common rebento (waist-to-chest-high gnarled root creature, pointed bark plates, amber chest core, two long clawed arms, rooted legs). NO new enemies, no tree boss. No other people. Natural clear combat geography, no teleportation, maintain shield left and sword right. Show wood chips and dust rather than blood. This is an inexperienced traveler learning a two-hit attack, not an invincible warrior.
SEVEN panels, easy left-to-right reading: wide top action panel, two medium panels row 2, two medium panels row 3, one wide panel row 4, one wide panel bottom. Keep all narration boxes comfortably inset; exact Brazilian Portuguese text below, large readable lettering with accents.
Panel 1 WIDE: first root claw strikes FRONT of raised LEFT shield. Hero braces, staggered one step backward, RIGHT sword low and angled away; clear impact on the outer shield, not blade blocking. Caption "O primeiro golpe atingiu o escudo." Small SFX "TUM!"
Panel 2: hero starts lowering his left shield and raises the right-hand sword to counter, worried face; creature's SECOND arm is visibly winding up at frame edge, threatening him. Caption "Baixei a espada para responder…"
Panel 3: same hero rapidly raises LEFT shield again, second claw hits its iron rim, body twists from force. Right sword remains drawn. Caption "…mas a outra garra já vinha." Small SFX "TAC!"
Panel 4: readable three-quarter view of root creature recovering from both swings, front bark plates part and expose amber resin chest; hero watching closely at edge. Caption "A madeira do peito se abriu enquanto ele recuperava o equilíbrio."
Panel 5: one precise RIGHT-handed sword slash into exposed wooden chest while hero's LEFT shield guards his body, strong clear diagonal action, bark chips fly; no gore, no cutting off the creature's head. Caption "Entrei nesse espaço e golpeei."
Panel 6 WIDE: a later finishing moment after learning the rhythm, root creature collapses into a low tangle of splintered limbs, amber glow fading. Hero standing a step away, exhausted, both weapons still correctly held, looking cautiously down at it. Caption "Na segunda tentativa, eu já sabia que eram dois golpes."
Panel 7 WIDE BOTTOM: quiet overhead-close view of THREE irregular grooves in the brown forest earth, clearly neither cart tracks nor boot prints, continuing between fern roots into the forest. Protagonist crouches at one side with left shield strapped to arm and right-hand sword pointed safely away from his legs, studying the grooves. Dead creature's bark fragments just behind. Caption "Três sulcos seguiam pela terra. Nenhum parecia feito por rodas."
Use cinematic directional movement and expressive hands; do not duplicate protagonist inside any one panel. Monster stays same size and silhouette as reference page 2. Narration never covers the sword, shield impact or faces. Clean panel separation, no additional text, no interface icons. Preserve subtle wonder and danger of the first two pages.
